title: Failure-to-Learn Review: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: Site leadership, top management and the board
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document; draft: the investigation status is in progress

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the ProbeMatrix investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate before adoption.
The export mentions regulator involvement but its summary sheet says 'Reportable to Regulator: No'. Confirm the reporting status with the organisation; this pack does not decide it.
The seal-repair history quotes a gasket change dated 18/09/2019; the evidence item notes that the narrative dates it 18/09/2020. The 2019 entry is left out of the missed opportunities.

bottom_line.text: Warnings were on record from 2011 onwards, and each one stalled at a step of the learning cycle rather than with one person.
Reporting: repeat seal failures on the meter that later leaked were closed as routine jobs and never reported as a warning.
Planning and intervening: known wall loss had no corrective plan, and overdue audit actions were extended without the approval the procedure required.
Evaluating: no step checked that a job or a drill had worked, so the system never learned that it had not.

sections.heading: Where the learning cycle broke
sections.intro: One row per phase of Drupsteen's five-phase learning-from-incidents cycle. Each row says what the export shows at that phase.

rows: Repeated seal jobs on meter 1 from November 2018 were each closed as routine maintenance, and none was reported as a reliability concern. The malfunction notification raised on 17 September 2020 was not closed or reviewed after the job.

No root-cause review of the repeat seal failures is recorded. The 2018 and 2019 internal safety audits gave observations without filled checklists, and the self-audit checklist was not specific to the plant, so the audits could not show what they had checked.

The 2017 thickness report asked for corrective action on pipes with significant wall loss; three years later no plan had been developed. The pitting found on the 36-inch line in July 2019 was answered with painting, and the record says the adequacy of painting still needed to be examined. The analysis also classes the display-only gas detection, the hand-operated isolation valves and the emergency plan's missing isolation criteria as known problems left uncorrected; the export does not date when each became known.

Of the 308 recommendations of the February 2018 external audit, 296 were complied with; the rest were extended to 30/04/2021 without the approval the procedure required. The management-of-change procedure published in August 2016 had not been used for plant changes since 2018.

No step checked that a job or an exercise had done what it was for. The notification for meter 1 was not reviewed after the job, the meter went back into service after pressurisation to operating pressure only, and the fire-drill records in SAP held no actions or observations.

sections.heading: Missed opportunities
sections.intro: Eleven dated warnings from 2011 to the week of the release, each tied to a finding that cites an earlier recommendation or a known problem left uncorrected. A year-only date means the source gives only the year.

events.text: Pipe-wall thickness measured in 2011, and next in 2017, against a four-year schedule.
events.response: None recorded: the slipped schedule was not escalated.
events.knowable_then: The schedule and the dates of the last measurements were in the inspection records.

events.response: Not applied to the 2018 header change, and not used for any change after that.
events.knowable_then: The procedure was a published site document.

events.text: External safety audit: most recommendations closed, the rest given later target dates.
events.response: Target dates extended to 30/04/2021 with no record of the approval the procedure required.
events.knowable_then: The audit report and its open recommendations were on record.

events.text: A gas header change is made without the management-of-change procedure.
events.response: None recorded: no change after this went through it.
events.knowable_then: The change records would show whether a change went through the procedure.

events.text: Meters 1 and 2 cleaned, serviced and calibrated: the first entry in the recorded seal history of meter 1.
events.knowable_then: The job was in the maintenance history.

events.text: The internal safety audit again records observations without a filled checklist.
events.knowable_then: The audit report showed that no checklist was filled.

events.text: Meter 1 cleaned and its gasket changed again.
events.response: Closed as routine maintenance; no root-cause review recorded.
events.knowable_then: The repeat job on the same meter was in the maintenance history.

events.text: Heavy pitting and wall loss found on a segment of the 36-inch pipeline.
events.response: Painted in December 2019; whether painting was enough was not examined.
events.knowable_then: The spot thickness measurement was recorded.

events.text: Calibration setting on meter 310FT01 changed and changed back, with no entry in the signed calibration documents.
events.knowable_then: The work was done under a calibration job; the signed record did not show the change.

events.text: Malfunction notification raised for meter 1 in SAP.
events.response: Gasket replaced the next day; the notification was not closed or reviewed after the job.

events.text: Gasket replaced and the meter pressurised to operating pressure only, with no hydro test.
events.knowable_then: The job record showed that no hydro test was done.

items.text: Fitting a locally bought O-ring in place of the original gasket became the regular practice on meter 1. Each seal job solved the day's leak and was closed as routine, so the repeat never looked like a change that needed review.

What the documents said and what the site did moved apart in small steps: a change procedure that stopped being used, drill results kept in an informal parallel record, and audits that recorded compliance without the data behind it. No single decision made the gap.

items.lesson: A repeat failure on the same item needs a route that reports it as a warning, not as another job.
items.explanation: The seal jobs on meter 1 were each recorded and closed as routine maintenance [FND-82FC718D; FND-3A34BAD3; EVD-1494]. The analysis states that the risk of the recurring failure was never assessed [FND-E0AE86A6]: no step in the maintenance records turned the repeats into a review.

items.lesson: An audit that records no checklist cannot find what it did not look at, so its silence is not assurance.
items.explanation: The 2018 and 2019 internal audits gave observations without a filled checklist [FND-5BA62765; EVD-7681], and the self-audit checklist was generic to the location [FND-C9C77FB7; EVD-9692]. Without a record of what was checked, the audits could not turn the plant's defects into findings.

items.lesson: A finding that needs corrective action needs a plan with an owner, or measurement becomes the response.
items.explanation: The 2017 thickness report called for corrective action, and three years later no plan existed [FND-0F19C9FC; FND-30D45EFE; EVD-5527]. When wall loss was found on the 36-inch line, painting was accepted as the fix without examining whether it was enough [FND-6E13192C; EVD-2397].

items.lesson: Extending an overdue safety action needs the approval the procedure sets, or the extension becomes the norm.
items.explanation: Most recommendations of the February 2018 external audit were complied with; the rest were extended to 30/04/2021 with no record of the required approval [FND-2A77BAFB; FND-9078AFA4; EVD-6852]. No record shows that the role with that authority accepted the delay.

items.lesson: A published procedure is a learning only while it is used; when it falls out of use, the change it guarded goes unreviewed.
items.explanation: The management-of-change procedure was published in August 2016 and, as the record states, no change went through it after 2018 [FND-922A04DB; FND-F7FE8463; EVD-2986]. The substitute seal on meter 1 was therefore never reviewed as a change [FND-CDE8E62D].

items.lesson: The learning cycle closes only when someone checks that a job or an exercise did what it was for.
items.explanation: The notification for meter 1 was not closed or reviewed after the gasket job, and no role was assigned to review it [FND-646BAC1F; FND-30C43927; EVD-0591]. Fire-drill records held no actions or observations [FND-BC32F8F7; EVD-2130], so neither could show whether anything had improved.

items.text: This review knows that meter 1 leaked on 24 September 2020; the people at the time did not. Every missed opportunity says what the record showed at that moment, events whose meaning was clear only afterwards are left out, and each learning asks why the system did not turn a warning into a change, not who missed it.

limits: The missed opportunities are the warnings the export dates; undated warnings in the findings are in the cycle table and the learnings only.
Earlier incidents at other sites are not in this export; the review covers this site's own records.
Some findings cite a recommendation of the post-incident committee rather than an earlier one; those are not treated as missed opportunities, because nobody could act on them before the event.
